reason: Employers can't be saved by the state. Pay what's owed, let a buyer take the shops, and keep tax out of it.
I ran things for years. Pay the workers their due, then let the market sort the shops. Councils run shops badly.
Workers first, always. I'd not trust a council with shops either. Pay people and let the chain go.
Give staff and the council first go at a shop. Cheap to try, and I'd rather see it reopen than sit empty.
Our town has empty shops already. Let the people who work there and the council have first call.
Workers and shoppers owning a shop sounds fair. Public loans are fine if they have to pay back.
I'd back staff owning their shop. Let people who use it have a vote, with the books published.
A short first right for staff and councils keeps shops open without paying the owners. That is sensible.
I need the workers paid quickly. Shops cannot be my first worry when wages are owed.
No taxpayer money for shops. Pay wages the law already promises, and leave the rest to buyers.
People who lost their jobs must get paid. Everything else is a gamble with other people's money.
Staff know the shop better than any rival. First call for them and the council is fair and cheap.
